Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for 2 days of constant dull lower abdominal ache with nausea and subjective fever (hot/sweaty), urinary frequency without dysuria/urgency, and recent slight pink discoloration in urine; plan for same-day in-person GP assessment to examine and perform pregnancy testing and further investigations; safety-netting provided.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Constant dull ache below the umbilicus for the last 2 days.
  - Nausea without vomiting.
  - Feeling hot and sweaty (subjective temperature).
  - Increased urinary frequency without pain, urgency, or foul odor.
  - Noted slight pink discoloration in urine over the last couple of days; uncertain if hematuria vs menstrual spotting (patient due for menses).
- Timeline:
  - Lower abdominal ache and nausea began ~2 days ago, gradual onset.
  - Constipation about 1 week ago, now resolved; normal bowel motion yesterday.
  - LMP ~3+ weeks ago; expecting period soon.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Positive: Nausea, urinary frequency, subjective fever/hot and sweaty, mild pink urine.
  - Negative: No vomiting, no diarrhea, no dysuria, no urgency, no foul-smelling urine, no vaginal discharge, no light-headedness/presyncope.
- Sexual/gynecologic:
  - Sexually active with one regular partner.
  - Contraception: contraceptive implant (Implanon).
  - LMP ~3+ weeks ago; period expected soon.
- Systems review (pertinent negatives noted above).

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported.

Medications:
- Contraceptive implant (Implanon) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No other medications reported.

Allergies:
- Amoxicillin.

Social History:
- Lives with boyfriend.
- Non-smoker.
- Alcohol and other substances: not discussed.

Family History:
- Brother with type 1 diabetes.
- No other familial diseases reported.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed (telehealth). No vitals documented.

Investigations:
- None performed during this telehealth visit.
- Plan: In-person evaluation with pregnancy test; further examinations/tests as indicated.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Lower abdominal pain with nausea, subjective fever, and urinary frequency
  - Assessment: Etiology unclear. Differential includes early pregnancy (including ectopic), urinary tract pathology, gynecologic causes (impending menses/spotting), and less likely constipation (now resolved).
  - Plan:
    - Same-day in-person GP assessment for abdominal/pelvic exam.
    - Urine pregnancy test to rule out pregnancy.
    - Further tests as indicated after exam (not specified in transcript).
- Issue 2: Possible hematuria vs menstrual spotting
  - Assessment: Patient observed pink-tinged urine; uncertain source (urinary vs vaginal), occurring just before expected menses.
  - Plan:
    - Clarify source on exam; consider urine dipstick/microscopy if indicated (not explicitly ordered in transcript).
- Safety-netting/Follow-up:
  - Attend in-person evaluation today as advised.
  - Seek urgent care if symptoms worsen, if light-headedness develops, or if any new concerning symptoms arise.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - No vitals; no physical exam findings.
  - No objective temperature; no pain severity score.
  - No urinalysis, STI screening history, pregnancy test result, or imaging.
  - Limited gynecologic/obstetric history (cycle regularity, prior pregnancies, STIs, pelvic pain history) not obtained.
  - Alcohol and other substance use not documented.
  - Full medication reconciliation not completed (OTC/herbals not asked).
- Internal conflicts:
  - Symptom duration stated as “last 2 days” by patient; doctor summarized “3 days” at one point (conflict noted).
  - Pink urine vs spotting: patient unsure if discoloration is hematuria or menstrual spotting (uncertainty noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Minor inaudible/unclear segments and repetitions; overall history obtainable but some details remained vague.
